title: Modi Brands Congress a 'Backstabber' Over DMK Betrayal
excerpt: PM fires sharpest salvo yet at Congress after it ditches 30-year Tamil Nadu ally DMK for actor-politician Vijay's party
body:
**What Happened:**

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on May 10 launched a blistering attack on the Indian National Congress in Bengaluru, accusing the opposition party of 'betraying' allies and people alike, while describing it as a 'parasitic political force' surviving at the expense of regional parties. The trigger: Congress had just abandoned its three-decade alliance with Tamil Nadu's DMK to back Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam — the party of actor-turned-politician C. Joseph Vijay — who was sworn in as Tamil Nadu's Chief Minister the same day.

**The Details:**

Congress contested the April 23 Tamil Nadu elections as part of the DMK-led Secular Progressive Alliance and won five seats, then extended support for Vijay after the TVK ended up as the single-largest party but fell short of the majority figure of 118. Congress got no berth in Vijay's nine-member cabinet — a pointed snub after delivering the votes that put him over the top. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi attended the swearing-in ceremony at Nehru Indoor Stadium in Chennai.

**Why It Matters:**

Sources in the DMK, led by former Chief Minister MK Stalin, had also used the 'backstabber' label after Congress threw its support behind the TVK — meaning Modi's language echoes the wounded ally itself, not just opposition spin. The move has reportedly annoyed the party's other national allies, such as the Samajwadi Party in Uttar Pradesh, with BJP national spokesperson Shehzad Poonawalla saying the developments reflect a growing 'distrust' among the allies of the Opposition INDIA bloc towards Congress. The episode hands BJP a ready-made narrative heading into future state elections: that the INDIA alliance is fracturing from within.

> *'Driven by its lust for power, the power-hungry Congress stabbed the DMK in the back at the very first opportunity. Now, Congress needs yet another party, one on whose back it can ride, to remain politically relevant.'*
> — PM Narendra Modi, addressing BJP workers at HAL Airport, Bengaluru, May 10, 2026

**Context:**

*For 25 to 30 years, Congress and the DMK shared a close relationship, with the DMK alliance repeatedly pulling Congress out of crises — indeed, the Congress-led UPA government that ruled for ten years before 2014 survived largely because of the DMK. Modi made his remarks during his visit to Karnataka for the 45th anniversary celebrations of the Art of Living Foundation. The DMK, founded in 1949, is Tamil Nadu's principal Dravidian party and currently the principal opposition force in the state assembly after losing the 2026 elections to TVK.*

**For the Diaspora:**

*The unravelling of the DMK-Congress alliance is a live stress test for India's opposition INDIA bloc — the coalition that millions of Indian-Americans who follow Indian democracy had hoped would mount a cohesive national challenge to the BJP.*

**What to Watch:**

With several key state elections and future national political battles ahead, political exchanges between the BJP and opposition parties are expected to become sharper in the coming months. Watch whether Congress is similarly frozen out by other INDIA bloc allies — particularly the Samajwadi Party in Uttar Pradesh — as intra-opposition tensions escalate.
